title: dispatch prepare resolves a cell's payload from its recorded tier
action: In prepare.rs prepare_dispatch: for kind == "cell", load the cell record BEFORE computing tier_token (the cell is already loaded for prompt context; move that load up if needed) and read its `tier` field. tier_token = the cell's tier when it is a non-empty string, else slot_for_kind(kind). Record tier_source: "cell" or "default" in the economics object. When the cell's tier is "ceiling": do NOT call resolve_tier — build the claude Agent-tool payload exactly like the native arm but with no `model` param and the prompt opening with `[bee-tier: ceiling]`, channel = "session-model", enforcement = "session-model"; for runtime codex, the spawn_agent arm likewise with no model. When the cell's tier names a tier with no configured slot in models.<runtime> (e.g. "extraction" missing), return a typed refusal {ok:false, type:"refused", reason:"tier_not_configured", tier, fix} — never fall back to generation. Cells with no tier field render byte-identically to before (tier_source "default"). Add tests in tests.rs: recorded generation → same payload as before plus tier_source cell; recorded ceiling → tool Agent, no model, [bee-tier: ceiling] marker, channel session-model; no tier → tier_source default, payload unchanged; unconfigured tier → refusal. Reuse the fixture style already in tests.rs for prepare.
acceptance: A ceiling cell's prepare result carries channel session-model and an Agent payload with no herding command; economics carries tier_source; an unconfigured recorded tier is a typed refusal; drivers tests green.
